Key Terms:
Slack Variable: A variable added to a less-than-or-equal-to inequality constraint to transform it into an equality constraint. Feasible Region: The set of all points that satisfy all the constraints of a linear programming problem.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 4><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 5><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 30>

Vertex: A point where two or more constraint boundaries intersect in the feasible region of a linear programming problem.  In the Simplex method, optimal solutions are found at vertices.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 5><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 29>

Basic Variable: In the Simplex method, a variable that is expressed in terms of non-basic variables in a dictionary.  In a basic feasible solution, basic variables are non-negative.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 7><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 8><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 11><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 14><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 15><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 26><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28>

Non-basic Variable: In the Simplex method, a variable set to zero in a given iteration of the algorithm.  The values of the basic variables are determined by the values of the non-basic variables.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 7><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 8><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 11><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 14><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 15><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 26><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28>

Pivot Operation: The process of exchanging a basic and a non-basic variable in the Simplex method, leading to a new basic feasible solution.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 14><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 15><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28>

Dictionary: A representation of a linear programming problem where basic variables are expressed as functions of non-basic variables.  It is used in the Simplex method to systematically move from one vertex to another.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 26><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 29>

Auxiliary Problem: A modified linear programming problem introduced to find an initial feasible solution when the origin is not feasible in the original problem. Problem Types:
Finding an Initial Feasible Solution:  The Simplex method requires an initial feasible solution.  If the origin is not feasible, an auxiliary problem is introduced to find a feasible solution to the original problem. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 32><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 33><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 34><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 35><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 36><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 37><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 38><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 39><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 40><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 41><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 42>

Handling Infeasible Origins:  The origin $(0, 0)$ may not satisfy all constraints in a linear programming problem.  Techniques like introducing an auxiliary problem are used to find a feasible starting point. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 30><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 32><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 33><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 34><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 35><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 36><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 37><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 38><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 39><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 40><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 41><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 42><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 43>

Optimizing in Higher Dimensions: The Simplex method is extended to solve linear programming problems with more than two variables, requiring iterative pivoting operations to move between vertices of the feasible region in higher-dimensional space. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 17><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 18><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 19><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 20><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 21><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 22><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 23><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 24><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 25>

Using Dictionaries to Represent Solutions:  The Simplex method uses dictionaries to represent the current solution and to perform pivot operations efficiently.  Each dictionary corresponds to a vertex of the feasible region. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 26><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 29>
Algorithm Solutions:
Simplex Method: Iteratively move from one vertex of the feasible region to another by setting non-basic variables to zero and choosing a new set of (non)basic variables to improve the objective function value. This is equivalent to moving from vertex to vertex in the feasible region. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 7><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 8><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 11><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 14><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 15><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 17><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 18><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 19><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 20><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 21><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 22><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 23><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 24><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 25>

Auxiliary Problem: When the origin is not feasible, introduce a new variable $x_0$ and modify the constraints to create an auxiliary problem that maximizes $-x_0$. Solve this auxiliary problem using the Simplex method. If the optimal solution has $x_0 = 0$, then the solution is feasible for the original problem. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 32><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 33><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 34><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 35><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 36><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 37><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 38><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 39><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 40><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 41><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 42><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 43>
